newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Golkar well ahead in poll count.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Golkar well ahead in poll count.

text.p: Indonesia's ruling Golkar had just over 87 percent of the ballots counted by 8:50 p.m. (1350 GMT) after Thursday's general elections, a statement issued by the election committee showed.
The statement said Golkar, in power for most of President Suharto's 30-year rule, had 7,127,499 of the 8,188,307 votes counted.

Of the other two parties legally permitted to contest the poll for 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives, the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) had 893,968 votes and the badly-split Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) 166,840.
This gave Golkar 87.04 percent, the PPP 10.92 and the PDI 2.04 percent.

Nearly 125 million people were eligible to vote in elections for the national parliament and regional and local assemblies. Golkar won 68 percent of the total vote in the last elections in 1992, the PPP 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.

The PPP expects to do well in its traditional support areas, including Jakarta and Central Java, and political analysts have expressed concern that party activists might not accept the outcome if the PPP was swamped in the polls.
